articles.title: $7 billion green boost: Amazon invests big in India's renewable energy landscape
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amazon is set to pump an additional $7 billion into renewable energy projects in India by 2030, taking its investments in the country's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amazon is set to pump an additional $7 billion into renewable energy projects in India by 2030, taking its investments in the country's carbon-free energy sector further as it expands its wind and solar power portfolio.The fresh investment comes on top of the $4 billion in renewable energy projects that the company has already contracted in India. Amazon said its existing projects, once operational, will have the capacity to generate enough electricity to meet the annual requirements of more than 3.5 million Indian households.According to the company's statement, Amazon has signed agreements for four new wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of 934 megawatts (MW). The projects are spread across Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.Karnataka will host two of these projects, including a 234 MW wind farm and a 200 MW project combining solar and wind energy. The wind farm is Amazon's largest wind energy project contracted in Asia so far. The other projects comprise a 300 MW solar facility in Madhya Pradesh and a 200 MW solar project in Rajasthan.The projects are backed by power purchase agreements, which involve long-term commitments to purchase electricity generated by specific renewable energy facilities. They are part of Amazon's existing $4 billion contracted investment in the country. Once operational, the company's contracted projects will have a combined capacity of more than 2 gigawatts (GW).Amazon said the planned $7 billion investment would also contribute to its broader efforts to reduce the carbon intensity of electricity used across its global operations.Company targets 65% reduction in electricity-related carbon intensityAlongside its India investment announcement, Amazon has set a global target to bring down the carbon intensity of electricity powering its operations by 65% by 2030.This means the carbon emissions associated with each unit of electricity consumed by the company will be 65% lower than the levels recorded in its 2019 baseline.The target is part of Amazon's efforts towards meeting its Climate Pledge commitment of achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2040. The company said the goal comes at a time when global energy demand is growing.Commenting on the investment, Kara Hurst, Amazon's chief sustainability officer, said, “Our renewable energy investments in India reflect years of sustained effort, planning, and collaboration across the industry. This additional investment of $7 billion underlines our long-term commitment, helping bring additional wind and solar capacity online while contributing to India’s energy security and long-term renewable energy ambitions,”Hurst added, “By expanding access to renewable energy at scale, we aim to help meet India’s growing electricity demand, strengthen the country’s energy security, and contribute to its ambitious goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070.”57 renewable energy projects across IndiaAmazon's renewable energy presence in India extends beyond utility-scale projects. Its current portfolio comprises 14 large-scale wind and solar projects that feed carbon-free electricity into the grid, along with 43 solar installations at its own facilities.Together, these 57 projects contribute to the company's efforts to increase the availability of carbon-free electricity and expand renewable energy capacity in the country.The investments are also expected to support electricity supply beyond Amazon's own operations. New carbon-free energy projects add power to the grid that serves households, hospitals, educational institutions and businesses.The expansion of renewable energy projects also supports the modernisation of energy infrastructure, helps maintain stable and affordable electricity access over time and contributes to job creation and better grid reliability.Increasing investments in carbon-free energy and grid infrastructure can also help scale new technologies, encourage innovation and strengthen the wider energy ecosystem.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Powering towns on pig manure: How Denmark has transformed energy generation
articles.summary: Pigs are big business in Denmark. Now their waste is being turned into biogas, which powers the national grid.
articles.body:
As the world seeks to cut carbon emissions to slow global warming, livestock manure is driving Denmark’s energy transition.

Pigs are big business in the Scandinavian nation, accounting for a quarter of its food exports. There are as many as 12 million breeding pigs in the country at any one time – more than double the human population, and that ratio spirals if you account for 30 million more produced for slaughter and live export every year.

Managing pig and cattle waste has long been a significant challenge. According to the Danish Agriculture and Food Council, Denmark’s pig sector annually produces more than 17 million tonnes of manure, mostly liquid slurry, emitting considerable amounts of greenhouse gas in the form of methane and nitrous oxide.

However, Denmark has been engineering a biogas boom, developing facilities to convert livestock waste into renewable natural gas to power the national grid and transport, fuel homes and make fertiliser.

In just more than a decade, the country has upscaled a handful of small biogas operations into about 150 industrial-sized plants, with up to 70 percent of the processed raw materials coming from pig and cattle manure.

Today, Denmark has Europe’s highest share of biogas in its gas grid, at about 40 percent. And this has timely benefits, given the volatile oil and gas markets caused by the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran.

Sustainable fuel has been embraced on an industrial scale in the coastal town of Sonderborg in southern Denmark, boosted by an ambitious initiative called ProjectZero, which was established in 2007.

It aimed to create a carbon-neutral energy system by the end of 2029. So far, the combined use of renewables, industrial waste heat and biogas has cut energy-related carbon emissions by 79 percent.

“In a world marked by geopolitical uncertainty, energy has become an even more critical infrastructure,” ProjectZero CEO Allan Pilgaard-Jensen told Al Jazeera. “Societies need resilient, local energy solutions. ProjectZero is definitely about climate solutions, but it also helps give us energy independence.”

The large-scale Glansager and Kvaers biogas facilities in Sonderborg use approximately 850,000 tonnes of organic material annually, comprised primarily of livestock slurry supplemented by food waste and crop residues. Together, the two facilities produce enough biogas to cover all of the Sonderborg region’s annual gas demand.

There are concerns about the reliance on livestock to provide the bulk of the organic input for the biogas plants, however.

A report by NOAH Friends of the Earth Denmark and Foodrise argues that the dependence on pig and cow manure is creating a factory farm trap that maintains high livestock numbers.

NOAH’s Jacob Sorensen said Denmark must reduce its number of pigs to tackle the climate crisis and to protect public health and biodiversity. “Denmark claims climate leadership, but its current biogas strategy is moving in the wrong direction,” he said.

“Biogas props up factory farming of pigs and locks in pollution rather than contributing to the necessary phasing out of the sector.”

Sorensen added that money spent on expanding biogas could be better used to fund emission-free energy solutions, “such as wind turbines, solar panels, geothermal heat and energy-saving technologies.”

Leading industry groups like Biogas Denmark counter, however, that biogas addresses immediate climate and energy security challenges and mitigates unavoidable agricultural emissions that will soon become an economic priority for farmers.

In 2030, Denmark will become the first country to introduce a carbon tax on agriculture. Danish farmers will have to pay about 16 euros ($18) for every tonne of carbon dioxide they emit.

At Grasten Agricultural College near Sonderborg, new systems are being tested on a small scale which could reduce the potential toll on the farming community.

Students here walk to class among the livestock barns, tractor sheds and grain silos you’d expect to see on any farm. But here, too, a biogas plant helps power the college’s operations, as well as a state-of-the-art carbon capture unit that absorbs excess CO2, which would otherwise be emitted to the atmosphere when biogas is burned.

“For a long time, farming has been seen as part of the problem, and we would like to change that so that farming becomes part of the solution,” said college principal Bjarne Ebbesen.

“The students are learning and testing new ways of thinking about how to make agriculture sustainable and profitable,” he said. “We’re a kind of living laboratory to test how agriculture can reduce emissions.”

This is how it works: Manure from the farm’s 200 cows and 400 sows is fed into an on-site biogas plant where bacteria break it down to produce biogas. This biogas is then burned in gas engines to generate electricity for the farm and excess heat for the college buildings.

Instead of releasing exhaust CO2, produced during the biogas combustion, directly into the atmosphere, a small-scale capture unit extracts it from the flue gas and pipes it into an on-site storage tank. The CO2 can then be sold for industrial processes like beverage carbonation, refrigeration and food processing.

“Agricultural carbon capture can be scaled up across the country,” said Ebbesen. “And it then becomes a money-making opportunity. Carbon is being used in many different processes, so why shouldn’t farmers sell it as they sell milk, grain or meat?”

As critics point out, turning manure into fuel will not solve farming’s broader ecological carbon footprint. But it is evident in Sonderborg that the energy transition is not confined to wind turbines and solar panels. Here, the road to net zero is running straight through the farmyard, as slurry is turned into energy and carbon could become a marketable crop.

articles.title: SNL sketch 'Sister' put a funny frame on caregiving. Millions of women are living it.
articles.summary: A Saturday Night Live sketch dubbed "Sister" hit close to home for many female caregivers for their parents.
articles.body:
A Saturday Night Live sketch dubbed "Sister," which aired in this past weekend's episode, portrayed a middle-aged man talking to the camera about the challenges of caring for his aging father.

"My dad means the world to me, so when I noticed him start to slow down, I knew I needed to get him the best care possible," host John Mulaney said. "I didn't know where to turn. That's when I heard about Sister. Sister is a living, 24/7 healthcare provider that is completely free and also your sister.

"I don't have to worry about Dad getting the care and attention he needs because my sister will do it."

After it aired, the sketch lit up social media feeds and spurred countless texts among sisters around the country.

"It went viral, and we laugh because too many of us recognize this," Angela M. Antonelli, executive director of the Center for Retirement Initiatives at Georgetown University, told Yahoo Finance. "But it also sadly suggests that 'Sister' comes to the role completely free, which couldn't be more wrong.

"Caregivers, a majority of whom are women, bear the cost in lost jobs, paychecks, savings, and retirement security. That's the real hidden cost of caregiving."

Women lose more hours of work annually to caregiving than men, according to AARP. And female caregivers experience larger average losses in lifetime Social Security income than men do — $9,400 compared to $6,800.

"Millions of women are juggling careers and caring for others, often at a steep cost to their own financial security," said Rita Choula, senior director of caregiving at AARP Public Policy Institute. "That's a financial hit that can follow them long after caregiving ends, putting their own retirement security at risk."

The sketch continued: "Signing up couldn't be easier. No applications, no insurance forms. Simply text, 'Dad fell' to Sister, and she will quit her job, break her lease, and move halfway across the country to take care of him."

Women caregivers more often make sacrifices, including stopping work entirely, "which is really dangerous," said Maddy Dychtwald, president of consulting company Age Wave.

According to an Age Wave report, women do 62% of the caregiving, and more than 40% have reduced or stopped saving, compared with 35% of men.

Commenters on SNL's YouTube channel drove home the reality:

"So on point! Didn't think anyone would ever bring this up…"

"I instantly sent this to my sister … who lives with and takes care of my Mom. They both howled! … :)"

articles.title: US Gas Pump Price Hits Lowest Since March as Oil Supply Recovers
articles.summary: US gasoline pump prices fell to the lowest since March following a broader decline in oil markets this month.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- US gasoline pump prices fell to the lowest since March following a broader decline in oil markets this month.

National regular unleaded gasoline dropped to an average $3.78 a gallon, according to the American Automobile Association. Global oil prices have fallen in recent weeks on increased flows from the Persian Gulf and indications from President Donald Trump that he'll hold off on renewed attacks against Iran.

While the move lower will be a welcome relief to US consumers, pump prices remain well above prewar levels.

articles.title: Beatriz Álvarez: “El problema del fútbol femenino ahora no es el gasto, sino la generación de ingresos”
articles.standfirst: La presidenta de Liga F señala la fidelización del público y la profesionalización de los clubes como grandes retos de la competición, mientras Iraia Iturregi y Kiyomi Cerezo ponen el foco en las estructuras de formación y la visibilidad del talento femenino
articles.summary: La presidenta de Liga F señala la fidelización del público y la profesionalización de los clubes como grandes retos de la competición, mientras Iraia Iturregi y Kiyomi Cerezo ponen el foco en las estructuras de formación y la visibilidad del talento femenino
articles.body: El fútbol femenino español ha dado un salto de gigante en los últimos años, pero todavía tiene importantes desafíos por delante para consolidar su crecimiento. La detección del talento, la profesionalización de las estructuras y la necesidad de construir un modelo de negocio sostenible fueron algunos de los asuntos que se abordaron en la mesa “El fútbol que viene: talento, profesionalización y crecimiento sostenible”, durante la IV edición del Expansión & MARCA Business Forum, celebrado en el Espacio La Salle de la madrileña calle San Juan de la Salle, en un foro que se desarrolló en jornadas de mañana y tarde, patrocinado por la Comunidad de Madrid, IFEMA Madrid, Iberdrola, Unicaja, LaLiga, Ariete, Cellnex, DAZN y Philip Morris España. Un debate que contó con la participación de Manuel Rivero, juez de Disciplina de LaLiga; Beatriz Álvarez, presidenta de Liga F; Kiyomi Cerezo, Co-CEO del grupo T3N Sport & Investment y Managing Partner de WomanGoal; e Iraia Iturregi, segunda entrenadora de la selección española femenina. Uno de los mensajes más contundentes lo dejó Beatriz Álvarez, que hizo balance de los primeros cuatro años de Liga F como competición profesional. “Tenemos las bases sólidas. Podemos empezar a levantar la mirada y empezar a construir alturas”, explicó la presidenta, que identificó tres grandes retos: fidelizar al espectador, consolidar las relaciones comerciales y profesionalizar los clubes. Sobre el primero, reconoció que las grandes asistencias, con partidos que han reunido a más de 40.000 aficionados, “suelen ser casos aislados o partidos aislados de máximo interés”. Por eso, incidió en la necesidad de mejorar la experiencia del aficionado, desde la accesibilidad a los estadios hasta las actividades complementarias: “El día de partido va más allá del partido”. Álvarez también hizo hincapié en la necesidad de reforzar las estructuras de los 16 clubes de la competición, tanto desde el punto de vista deportivo como en la gestión del negocio. En este sentido, dejó una reflexión especialmente significativa sobre la sostenibilidad económica de Liga F: “El problema ahora no es el gasto, sino la generación de ingresos”. La presidenta defendió la importancia de incrementar los recursos disponibles para poder reinvertirlos en el crecimiento del fútbol femenino, además de apostar por la incorporación de profesionales especializados y departamentos dedicados exclusivamente a esta parcela dentro de los clubes. Desde la perspectiva de la detección del talento, Kiyomi Cerezo defendió la importancia de generar oportunidades para las futbolistas que todavía no tienen acceso a las grandes estructuras deportivas. “En nuestro caso apostamos mucho por la visibilidad”, señaló la co-CEO de WomanGoal, que explicó el trabajo desarrollado por su proyecto para conectar jugadoras con clubes y oportunidades profesionales. “En estos tres años hemos visto a 20.000 jugadoras”, destacó, explicando que alrededor de 60 futbolistas han conseguido nuevas oportunidades deportivas gracias a esa labor. Para Cerezo, visibilizar el talento desde las categorías formativas resulta fundamental para superar las barreras que todavía existen en numerosos territorios. Por su parte, Iraia Iturregi puso el foco en la evolución que ha experimentado la preparación de las futbolistas. “No es que las jugadoras entrenen más ahora, sino que tienen muchísimas más herramientas para entrenar mejor”, explicó la segunda entrenadora de España, que destacó la incorporación de especialistas en entrenamiento de fuerza, nutrición, psicología y análisis. Una transformación que también se aprecia en las nuevas generaciones, que llegan con mayores conocimientos tácticos, una mejor preparación física y “una mentalidad mucho más profesional”. Iturregi destacó, además, “el hambre que tienen de querer seguir ganando” las internacionales españolas, incluso después de conquistar títulos. Sin embargo, Iturregi advirtió de la necesidad de seguir reforzando las bases del fútbol femenino para mantener ese nivel competitivo. “La clave está en mejorar las estructuras de todo el mundo, los cuerpos técnicos, las instalaciones, la formación, las categorías inferiores”, defendió. Una apuesta que requiere paciencia y una visión a largo plazo: “Invertir en estructuras no se ve en el corto plazo”, recordó, insistiendo en la importancia de trabajar pensando en las futbolistas y las competiciones de dentro de cinco o diez años. La visión institucional la aportó Manuel Rivero, juez de Disciplina de LaLiga, que explicó la importancia de contar con mecanismos de resolución de conflictos en un entorno cada vez más profesionalizado. Rivero recordó que su cargo lo desempeña una persona externa a LaLiga y comparó a los 42 clubes del fútbol profesional con vecinos de un mismo edificio, donde conviven entidades con realidades económicas muy diferentes. Una perspectiva que puso sobre la mesa la complejidad de gestionar un ecosistema deportivo en constante transformación. Visibilidad, estructuras y recursos fueron, en definitiva, los tres grandes ejes de un debate que dejó una idea compartida: el talento necesita oportunidades, pero también clubes e instituciones preparados para convertir el crecimiento deportivo en un proyecto sostenible.

articles.title: Jorge de la Vega: "El consumo de fútbol es el mayor de la historia"
articles.standfirst: El director general de negocio de LaLiga, protagonista en la IV edición del Expansión & MARCA Business Sport Forum
articles.summary: El director general de negocio de LaLiga, protagonista en la IV edición del Expansión & MARCA Business Sport Forum
articles.body: Jorge de la Vega, director general de negocio de LaLiga, charló con Emilio Contreras, director adjunto de MARCA, en el segundo diálogo de la IV edición del Expansión & MARCA Business Sport Forum, en una mesa titulada 'Más allá de los 90 minutos: el nuevo modelo de negocio de LaLiga'. De la Vega charló sobre cómo pueden generar los clubes más recursos, nuevas audiencias y cómo generar interés más allá del partido en directo. El director general de negocio de LaLiga comenzó hablando de la fórmula de los clubes para generar más recursos más allá del partido en sí. "La principal misión de LaLiga tiene que ver con el crecimiento de los derechos audiovisuales, pero hemos tratado de seguir aumentando las oportunidades para los clubes. En lo que tiene que ver con los derechos, no solo importan los 90 minutos, sino que tenemos que ser capaces de dar oportunidades y ventanas, y en el ámbito que tiene que ver con el patrocinio, dar más visibilidad a las marcas", explicó. Además, apuntó a una parte no solo cuantitativa, sino también cualitativa: "Que las marcas puedan contarlo de manera diferente. Hemos pasado de un patrocinio mas clásico a una plataforma que permite contar historias. Alguna sucede en los 90 minutos y otras alrededor de todo lo que es la conversación de fútbol". De la Vega continuó explicando cómo transformar el fútbol en un negocio que dure siete días a la semana y 365 días al año. "El cambio que se produjo para pasar a jugar de viernes a lunes ya fue un gran cambio para intentar que la jornada fuera más larga y ofrecer a nuestros clientes la posibilidad de ofrecer más contenido. A partir de ahí, hay muchas fórmulas para ser relevante. Hay una cuestión del propio contenido audiovisual, de highlights, pero no queremos limitarnos solo a eso. De lo que se trata es de estar presentes en la vida de las personas con la mayor frecuencia posible. Sin olvidarnos del partido en directo, pero poniendo la atención no solo a eso, sino que tenemos que estar más pendientes en el día a día", reflexionó. Sobre cómo mejorar la experiencia del aficionado, también ofreció su punto de vista el dirigente de LaLiga. "De lo que se trata es de intentar tener más oportunidades de conectar con el aficionado. Hemos tratado de crear el mayor ecosistema de fútbol del mundo. Podemos decirlo con toda la humildad del mundo, pero al final de lo que se trata es de conseguir un objetivo multitarget, multiengagement y multicultural. Hay gente experta en LaLiga que se sabe todo sobre el Fantasy, pero también gente que ocasionalmente se junta con amigos y disfruta del fútbol", apuntó. De la Vega restó importancia a las diferencias de edad, aunque reconoció que no consumen de igual manera el fútbol. "La realidad es que hay una cierta confusión respecto a los análisis de cómo se comporta cada uno. Uno va consumiendo y cambiando sus consumos. El consumo de fútbol es el mayor de la historia. Pensar que porque un chaval mientras ve el partido está mirando el móvil y disfrutando del fútbol jugando a la consola va en detrimento del interés por la competición es un error, es todo lo contrario. Cuando hace un tiempo salió el debate de la Kings League... nosotros encantados de que la gente se aficione a un entretenimiento que tiene que ver con el fútbol. Nosotros intentamos hacer un producto para todos los públicos, tenemos un cliente principal y ese cliente en su día fue un niño", expuso. Los clubes tienen que competir por la tarta televisiva con otras competiciones y con otros sectores de entretenimiento. Para De la Venga, tienen una ventaja, y es el interés por el deporte en directo. "Tú compites por el tiempo de las personas y tienes una cierta limitación, porque cada uno de nosotros tenemos al día un número de horas de disfrute y de ocio, y ese tiempo lo reparte entre muchas cosas. Ahora hay multitud de opciones. El deporte en directo siempre va a tener algo diferente respecto a una película o una serie. Si hay algo que no para de crecer es el deporte y la música". Y se refirió a las tres patas del negocio de LaLiga: "Que sea bueno para el patrocinio, que sea bueno para LaLiga y que sea bueno para el fan: el triple win". En cuanto a los nuevos formatos, De la Vega cree que están obligados a estar pendientes de las novedades pero sin perder lo que les hace diferentes: "Siempre hay que estar pendiente de la novedad, si ves que al aficionado hay cosas que le van gustando tienes que estar pendiente. Tienes que tener ese punto de equilibrio de no perder tu esencia, pero siempre con una mirada innovadora de ver qué cosas hay en el mercado", aclaró. Por último, hizo una reflexión sobre el futuro, en concreto hacia dónde va LaLiga y dónde estará en el año 2040. "Ya hemos pasado 2030... estamos poniendo el ojo muy lejos. Habrá cosas que cambien, pero habrá cosas que seguirán siendo comunes. Estamos viendo el interés que generan los partidos en directo, con récord de asistencia a los estadios. El interés por el directo cada vez es mayor. Se acaba de disputar la NFL en el Bernabéu y ves cómo el partido no dura solo los 90 minutos. Además toda la cantidad de eventos, conciertos, etc que se pueden hacer, es una nueva forma de monetización pero para los equipos de LaLiga es interesante porque también es una manera de enseñar su marca y conectar con los aficionados de diferentes maneras. El deporte y la música van a estar siempre con nosotros. Hemos pasado la pandemia y estamos en el mejor momento", reflexionó De la Vega.

articles.title: Jensen Huang looks to have accepted his fate with Nvidia: He cleaned up his X profile
articles.summary: Jensen moving on with his life?
articles.body:
Jensen Huang appears to be accepting that he will not be returning to Nvidia ( NVDA ) as CEO.

At least, that's if you decode the move he just made on his X account.

Huang updated his profile on Tuesday, changing it to simply "founder" of Nvidia. It no longer has the Nvidia affiliation badge.

Huang first joined his friend Elon Musk's X on July 24, 2026, posting a letter he signed on why open models matter.

He has gone on to amass 1.3 million followers while sharing 21 posts.

The man who founded Nvidia in 1993 and turned it into the most important company in the AI revolution is coming up on a week since stepping down as CEO, following a period of explosive revelations and mounting controversy.

According to The New York Times, Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence has put Nvidia under an extraordinary spotlight.

The Times also reported that Huang had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, one of roughly 60 people who report directly to him.

Reuters reported last Thursday that Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, whose identity has not been disclosed.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title: North Bengaluru expansion puts focus on low-density residential projects
articles.summary: North Bengaluru has emerged as a key area of the city’s expansion over the past decade.
articles.body: North Bengaluru has emerged as a key area of the city’s expansion over the past decade. Developments around the airport, Metro connectivity, Manyata Tech Park and Phoenix Mall of Asia have contributed to the corridor’s growth, alongside an increase in residential development. As the area has expanded, there has also been growing interest in residential options that offer greater privacy and lower-density living.According to Krishnaiah Projects Pvt Ltd, Bollineni Vienna at Kogilu Cross in Yelahanka is planned around this demand for lower-density living. The company states that the project comprises over 80 residences spread across 2.65 acres, with two towers rising to G+18 floors. Krishnaiah Projects Pvt Ltd is the real estate arm of the 52-year-old Bollineni Group (BSCPL), according to the company.Fewer homes, more roomThe company states that the residences are available in 4 and 5 BHK configurations, ranging from 3365 to 5510 sq ft. Tower A has two homes per floor; Tower B has three. No residence shares a common wall with another, and a private elevator opens directly into each home. Layouts are 100 per cent Vastu-compliant. Close to 80 per cent of the site is left open, landscaped ground rather than built mass.“Ninety homes on 2.65 acres was a decision we took early and have not revisited,” says TV Manjunath, CEO. “Almost everything residents will value here, the open space, the privacy, the light through the day, follows from that one number. It is easier to add amenities later than to add distance between homes.”A clubhouse sized for the community, not the renderAccording to the company, the 25,000 sq ft clubhouse is planned as shared ground rather than an amenity list. It includes a double-height badminton court, a paddle pool, a gymnasium, a meditation deck, a jogging track, lawn tennis and pickleball courts, and a children's play area. A lounge and gathering plaza anchors the social side. The Herbarium and the Skyline Perch — a landscaped terrace and an elevated viewing deck — extend the community upward as well as outward.Connected, without sitting in the trafficKogilu Cross sits off Bellary Road, with the Outer Ring Road and Kempegowda International Airport both within a straightforward drive. Manyata Tech Park and Hebbal serve the working commute; Phoenix Mall of Asia and Yelahanka Junction cover the everyday one. The location gives access to North Bengaluru's infrastructure without placing residents inside its busiest stretches.A record behind the addressBollineni's real estate division has been building since 2012, averaging close to one and a half homes a day over that period.That pipeline sits against a broader shift in how buyers at this end of the market assess a home. articles.title: Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney dies at 95; started global chain with $600 loan from mother
articles.summary: Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney, who turned a $600 loan from his mother into one of the world's biggest pizza chains alongside his brother Frank, has died
articles.body: Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney, who turned a $600 loan from his mother into one of the world's biggest pizza chains alongside his brother Frank, has died at the age of 95.Carney died peacefully on November 13, surrounded by his family, according to an obituary published by his family. No cause of death was disclosed. The New York Post reported his death on Monday, citing the obituary.Carney and his brother Frank founded Pizza Hut in 1958 in Wichita, Kansas, when Dan was 26. The brothers borrowed $600 from their mother to set up their first restaurant, which opened near Wichita State University.The venture took off despite pizza being relatively unfamiliar to many American diners at the time. Within a year, the brothers began franchising the business, which subsequently expanded into an international restaurant chain.In 1977, PepsiCo acquired Pizza Hut for $300 million. Frank, who had served as the company's CEO, left the position in 1980. He died in December 2020 at the age of 82 after battling pneumonia.Who was Dan Carney?Born in Kansas City, Missouri, Carney grew up in a large family and was one of 12 siblings, according to the NYP. He graduated from Wichita State University in 1953 with a bachelor's degree in business administration.He subsequently served two years in the US Air Force as a first lieutenant before returning to his academic pursuits. He received his master's degree in 2004, 51 years after completing his undergraduate studies.Carney married his childhood sweetheart, Beverly Singleton, in February 1954. The couple had six children and 12 grandchildren. Beverly died in 1998. Carney later married Gayla Coulter in 2001, and she survives him.Beyond his business career, Carney was involved in philanthropy and served as chairman of the board of the Cerebral Palsy Research Foundation of Kansas for 50 years.His obituary described him as a leader known for his integrity, generosity and commitment to mentoring others.“Dan was revolutionary in the franchise world,” the obituary said, adding that he was an investor not just in businesses but also in people.Wichita State pays tributeWichita State University, Carney's alma mater, also paid tribute to the entrepreneur, recalling his contribution to the institution and the wider community.In a Facebook post on Monday, the university described him as an entrepreneur, philanthropist and proud Shocker whose impact would be felt for generations.The university also highlighted his humility, wisdom and belief in giving back, saying his mentorship had shaped the lives of students and colleagues.The original Pizza Hut building, where the brothers launched their business, has been preserved on the Wichita State campus. It now houses the Pizza Hut Museum, which opened to the public in 2018.Carney had attended the museum's opening and described seeing the original building as a humbling experience, according to a Wichita State University press release.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: JD.com beats profit expectations on cost cuts
articles.summary: Investing.com - JD.com Inc (NASDAQ:JD) on Tuesday reported third quarter results that met analyst expectations for earnings while revenue came in slightly be...
articles.body:
Investing.com - JD.com Inc ( JD )on Tuesday reported third quarter results that met analyst expectations for earnings while revenue came in slightly below estimates, as the Chinese e-commerce company returned to positive revenue growth while accelerating profit expansion.

The company posted adjusted earnings per ADS of RMB5.88 ($0.88) for the third quarter, matching the analyst consensus of RMB5.88. Revenue reached RMB309.6 billion ($46.2 billion), marginally below the estimate of RMB309.8 billion but up 3.5% YoY from RMB299.1 billion in the year-ago period.

"We delivered solid results in the third quarter, returning to positive revenue growth while accelerating profit growth," said Sandy Xu, Chief Executive Officer of JD.com. "This performance was underpinned by the resilience of JD Retail and continued loss reduction in New Businesses."

Adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders surged 44% YoY to RMB8.3 billion ($1.2 billion), compared to RMB5.8 billion in the third quarter of 2025. The company's adjusted operating margin expanded to 2.4% from 0.1% in the prior year period, driven primarily by a 26.2% reduction in marketing expenses.

JD Retail, the company's core segment, generated operating income of RMB15.1 billion ($2.2 billion) with a 5.8% operating margin, compared to RMB14.8 billion and a 5.9% margin in the year-ago quarter. New Businesses delivered meaningful loss reductions both YoY and sequentially, according to CFO Ian Su Shan.

Net product revenues increased 3.1% YoY while net service revenues grew 4.7%. The company completed its acquisition of 59.8% of CECONOMY AG on November 12, 2026, for EUR1,335 million, strengthening its presence in Europe.

articles.title: The Fed seems to be getting worried about AI
articles.summary: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said that the potential for higher unemployment and the dangers of bad actors using AI for nefarious purposes could be "highly disru...
articles.body:
Thinking through the potential consequences of the AI revolution isn't explicitly part of the Fed's dual mandate.

But the sweeping impacts of AI, and all the corners of the economy that the emerging technology is set to disrupt, have drawn increasing scrutiny from central bankers.

On Monday, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh kicked off the first task force hearing on how AI could juice GDP growth or lead to higher unemployment.

Warsh notably did not take the posture of industry booster or tech critic. "Our ‌role in all this is neither advocacy nor opposition," Warsh said. "Our job is to prepare for whatever comes next."

That means focusing on AI's possible impacts and considering different outcomes, ranging from broad-based economic gains to massive job displacement to an AI letdown and productivity slump.

Warsh noted that AI might be different from other paradigm-shifting technologies because of its propensity to generate new ideas and speed up the pace of innovation.

In the best scenario, Warsh told the Fed conference in San Francisco , the technology could lead "to an increase in productivity and economic gains that are shared broadly ‌across labor and the owners of ⁠capital. In that event, real GDP growth rises persistently above its long-run average, and the US stays close to full employment."

But given the Fed's specific objectives — inflation and employment — the risks overshadowed the optimism.

Warsh said that the potential for higher unemployment and the dangers of bad actors using AI for nefarious purposes could be "highly disruptive and economically costly."

The chair also referred to AI using the language preferred by Donald Trump and Elon Musk, calling it "super intelligence."

Other central bankers went further. Federal Reserve governor Michael Barr on Monday laid out an array of risks posed by AI . He elaborated on the dangers posed to the financial system if AI technology continues to advance and is widely adopted, such as AI-fueled bank runs, AI trading models that encourage herd-like behavior, and security concerns around autonomous agents exploiting vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Nvidia is being pulled in opposite directions by 2 powerful forces
articles.summary: Part of what has made Huang's reported affairs and resignation such a big story is that it contains so many competing storylines.
articles.body:
Everyone's social feeds are a little different. So depending on your own views towards China, open-weight AI models, Silicon Valley founders, and the role of Big Tech in society, the idea of Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia ( NVDA ) is a brilliant, righteous comeback, a threat to national security, or the height of corporate irresponsibility.

Nvidia is reportedly waving off the comeback. Its efforts are directed instead to the investigation into Huang and navigating a regulatory landscape that's more hostile to Chinese competition. But regardless of the company's public posture, it is being pulled in opposite directions by very powerful forces.

Much of the tech world is clamoring for Huang's return. Meanwhile, members of Congress are sharpening their oversight knives. And in an extraordinary show of Cabinet infighting, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to block China from getting ahold of Nvidia's most advanced chips.

Part of what has made Huang's reported affairs and resignation such a big story is that the saga contains so many competing storylines .

The drama criss-crosses tech, geopolitics, and business culture. You can imagine and have probably encountered Huang content on every social media platform, from TikTok skits of AI nerds getting tricked by "spy baddies," to LinkedIn posts remarking on the need for a strong corporate succession plan, and X threads on how the whole episode is a win for China hawks.

A sex scandal with the power to rattle the S&P 500 has the narrative juice to entice your politics-brained dad, your day-trading brother, and your Real Housewives-obsessed bestie.

But the varying interests drawing people to the story also highlight political and financial tensions that make Nvidia so important to the economy.

Huang is simultaneously occupying the role of founder hero, traitor to his country, China dove whipping boy, and free-market bulwark.

The competing narratives are proving too much for the stock. Tickers typically aren't supposed to become the stage for so much messiness. At least 10 analysts downgraded their Buy rating on Nvidia to Hold. Shares are down roughly 13% over the past week.

An earnings call after the bell will attract even more attention. Investors expect some clarity on the status of the search for a permanent CEO and Nvidia's role in China's acquisition of advanced AI tech. And, given the quarter's high expectations, like revenue nearly doubling from the same period last year, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus, the results will no doubt underscore the opposing forces pulling on the company.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI heads to launch amid feverish anticipation
articles.summary: By Aditya Soni, Matt Silverstein and Lisa Richwine Nov 17 (Reuters) - Vacation days have been booked. Millions of copies of the game have been preordered and...
articles.body:
By Aditya Soni, Matt Silverstein and Lisa Richwine

Nov 17 (Reuters) - Vacation days have been booked. Millions of copies of the game have been preordered and preloaded. One gamer even asked a spouse to promise, in writing, not to interrupt.

Take-Two Interactive's Rockstar Games' action-adventure video game series "Grand Theft Auto" returns on Thursday with its first new title ‌in 13 years and gamers are rearranging their lives to participate in a shared cultural moment rarely seen in this era of fragmented audiences. "Grand Theft Auto VI" is the ‌latest installment in a franchise that turned American excess into satire, outsold some of Hollywood's biggest blockbusters and drew the fury of lawmakers with its graphic violence.

"Everyone's talking about it, all my friends at work and just talking online ... it really feels ​like a whole societal coming together in a way," said Owen Donahue, a 23-year-old from Los Angeles who works in the TV industry.

"Grand Theft Auto" began in 1997 with a top-down, heavily pixelated game that involved stealing cars and carrying out jobs for crime syndicates. With each installment, the graphics and storyline became more sophisticated. GTA V, released in 2013 by Take-Two Interactive's Rockstar Games and set in an alternative Los Angeles called Los Santos, was one of the best-selling video games of all time.

But that was 13 years ago. The wait for the next one has been so long that it became a running joke in ‌gaming circles, with many players only children at the last launch. ⁠Every sliver of the title's footage has been devoured, from its first trailer that has drawn more than 300 million YouTube views since its release nearly three years ago, to an August gameplay preview that briefly crashed Netflix.

Paid time-off requests for launch day have been running about 13% higher than a normal November ⁠day, according to data from BambooHR, which runs a platform that helps small- and medium-sized businesses track schedules. Further employees are likely to call in sick on Thursday, it says. A BambooHR survey of 1,500 US adults found about one-third of Gen Z workers plan to take the day off.

"This is at a scale and size that we have not seen in other entertainment launches," said BambooHR CEO Brad Rencher.

Singaporean gamer Julian Tay said ​in ​a social media post that he had drawn up a five-point "GTA VI Gaming Agreement" for his spouse, covering the ​first 10 days after launch and stipulating when missions could be interrupted and ‌when hugs, kisses and errands were allowed.

articles.title: Home Depot taps Richard McPhail as new CEO, reports Q3 earnings beat
articles.summary: Current CEO Ted Decker will stay on as board Chair, while CFO Richard McPhail will be named CEO.
articles.body:
Home Depot ( HD ) beat Wall Street's metrics across the board in the third quarter and adjusted its full-year outlook amid a shake-up in its C-suite leadership.

The company announced that Richard McPhail, who joined the company in 2005 and currently serves as CFO, will become CEO on Nov. 23. Current CEO Ted Decker has returned from temporary medical leave and will continue to serve as chair of the board, Home Depot said.

Jordan Broggi, a 13-year veteran of Home Depot, will take the CFO role, while senior executive vice president Ann-Marie Campbell was promoted to president and COO.

In the third quarter, revenue grew by nearly 5% to $43.4 billion, above the $42.8 billion analysts forecast, per Bloomberg estimates. Adjusted earnings per share grew 3% to $3.86, more than the $3.85 predicted.

"Results in the third quarter exceeded our expectations," incoming CEO McPhail said in the release. "Our associates' strong engagement and exceptional execution, combined with our continued investments across the business, enabled us to grow market share in a dynamic environment."

Home Depot stock declined slightly in premarket trading following the announcement.

Same-store sales increased 2.2%, more than the roughly 1.7% expected, and US same-store sales also jumped 2.2%, higher than the 1.5% expected.

The company said the average ticket size increased by 3% due to a mix of inflation and some customers trading up to new and innovative products. But customers had fewer visits to Home Depot stores.

Home Depot said it saw strength in its power department, which saw double-digit growth, as well as in storage, plumbing, and electrical, which grew by mid-single-digit percentages.

The company adjusted its 2026 forecast. It now expects total sales to grow by 4.5%, at the high end of its previously expected range for the year, and expects its same-store sales growth outlook to be up 1.4%, toward the higher end of its previously expected range of flat to up 2%.

Lowe's ( LOW ) is expected to post a same-store sales increase of 0.4% when it reports quarterly results on Wednesday.

articles.title: El circuito de Madring cambiará en 2027 "para aquellos que se quejan de que no hay adelantamientos"
articles.standfirst: José Vicente de los Mozos, presidente ejecutivo de IFEMA Madrid, lo desveló en el Expansión & MARCA Business Sport Forum
articles.summary: José Vicente de los Mozos, presidente ejecutivo de IFEMA Madrid, lo desveló en el Expansión & MARCA Business Sport Forum
articles.body: Como no podía ser de otra forma, la Fórmula 1 tuvo su cuota de protagonismo en la IV edición del Expansión & MARCA Business Sport Forum, con una mesa titulada 'Fórmula 1 en España: el motor de la transformación urbana. Caso de éxito internacional'. Durante 45 minutos debatieron José Vicente de los Mozos, presidente ejecutivo de IFEMA Madrid y promotor de Madrid Gran Premio de Madrid de Fórmula 1; Carmelo Sanz, presidente del RACE y vicepresidente de la FIA; y Eugenio Blanco, senior vice president Content de DAZN España. De los Mozos ofreció la gran noticia de la mesa al desvelar que el circuito de Madring tendrá novedades de cara al próximo año. "Este es un punto de partida, no de llegada. Nadie esperaba ver lo que vio en Madrid. ¿Qué hay que hacer? Cinco cosas. Una, mejorar los accesos. Dos, ampliar el programa de entretenimiento. Tenemos pabellones donde se pueden hacer eventos después. Hay pabellones vacíos y que yo sepa el asfalto no da dinero. Tres, mejorar la experiencia de hospitality. Cuatro, seguir ampliando la oferta turística, cultural y gastronómica de Madrid. Y además, ya hemos modificado el circuito. Aquellos que se quejan de que no hay adelantamientos, habrá modificaciones, hay una chicane. Habrá una curva que será muy emblemática que va a gustar. Eso ya está hecho. Tenemos más sorpresas que iremos diciendo en las próximas semanas y meses", anunció. El presidente ejecutivo de IFEMA, además, dio un tirón de orejas al Gobierno. "2027 va a ser mejor que 2026 porque vamos a hacer mejoras. Las encuestas superan el 90% de gente que dice que su experiencia fue maravillosa, que recomiendan venir y que van a volver. El año pasado hubo empresas que llegaron tarde a hospitality por el Mundial de fútbol. Después del Mundial y los Juegos Olímpicos, lo principal es la Fórmula 1. Este año no hay ni Mundial ni Juegos Olímpicos. En 2026 han venido 352.600 y vamos a ir a por ello. El ingreso son sponsors y ticketing. No entiendo por qué Montmeló tiene una exención especial fiscal y Madrid no. Espero que con el nuevo gobierno lo tengamos, igual que Barcelona. Estamos en el mismo país". También tuvo tiempo para tirar de humor: "El segundo día todos los mecánicos sabían decir 'Joselito" (en referencia a los jamones). De los Mozos ofreció algunos datos que refuerzan la celebración del Gran Premio de Madrid: "2771 euros de gasto medio de los turistas internacionales, 1,7% más de media que un turista normal. El día anterior tuvimos una página en el New York Times, ¿hace cuánto que España no tiene una página en el New York Times?". Antes de dar la noticia de que Madring cambiará el próximo año, José Vicente de los Mozos explicó cómo se gestó el Gran Premio de Madrid: "En Europa había muchas carreras de Fórmula 1 pero no había ningún espectáculo de Fórmula 1. A mi me dijeron 'pero si tenemos 10 países en el mundo antes que tú'. ¿Qué les ofrecimos? Una experiencia. Es el circuito en el que menos se tarde desde un hotel de lujo en el centro al circuito. Hemos creado algo que nadie tiene, los garajes son los mejores del circuito, con aire acondicionado. El éxito no es solo usar la semana de la Fórmula 1, sino cómo utilizamos esas instalaciones. No ha nacido Madrid para competir con el Jarama, Madrid tiene su hoja de ruta y Jarama tiene la suya. Que Madrid haya tenido la Fórmula E y la F1 en el mismo año, es un éxito". Carmelo Sanz, por su parte, alabó a Madrid por convertirse "en la capital mundial de la movilidad y de motorsport". "Madrid este año de forma inteligente ha alineado a los políticos, hemos conseguido que tanto el ayuntamiento como la Comunidad nos hayan apoyado en convertir Madrid en la capital mundial de la movilidad y de Motorsport. Tiene mucho mérito y por si le faltaba algo de credibilidad a Madrid en organizar grandes eventos, esto es poner la guinda. Tener dos campeonatos del mundo significa mucho. No se nos puede olvidar que esto no es solo una competición deportiva, hay una industria que es la industria del automóvil. Casi hemos garantizado que en el 2027 vamos a estar trabajando duro de nuevo". Sanz explicó su aportación al Gran Premio de Madrid. "¿Qué ha hecho el RACE en este Gran Premio? Lo que nadie ve, organizar la seguridad en la pista. Todos los servicios médicos, comisarios, bomberos... Hemos aportado nuestra experiencia a un circuito urbano y ayudar en lo que hemos podido. Ha sido un gran éxito". Eugenio Blanco ofreció la visión audiovisual del asunto desde el punto de vista de DAZN. "Sabíamos que esta carrera iba a ser especial, por la novedad, el carácter de Madrid, que IFEMA quería introducir novedades. Había una gran experiencia social, de VIPS, que teníamos que contar. La Fórmula 1 es un derecho central de nuestro catálogo. Es el derecho que nos pone en el mapa de la gran audiencia en España. La Fórmula 1 nos ha dado una dimensión superior antes de entrar en el fútbol y adquirir los derechos de LaLiga. Tiene una capacidad de captar horas de consumo muy significativas. Captamos al gran espectador de la Fórmula 1 pero también entró una nueva generación. La Fórmula 1 tiene todas las grandes esencias deportivas del héroe, la adrenalina...". Blanco se refirió a que la forma de contar la historias son casi tan importantes como las propias historias. Ahora tenemos al mejor piloto de la parrilla con 44 años y a un campeón del mundo de 19 años. Son dos historias potentísimas, dos generaciones en colisión. Las historias deportivas. Y luego vamos a los formatos. Una vez que tienes las historias deportivas o humanas, en esta pelea del universa mediático, es qué historia funciona mejor en cada una de las plataformas".

articles.title: Who is new Home Depot CEO Richard McPhail?
articles.summary: Home Depot has a new CEO. Here's what we know.
articles.body:
Home Depot ( HD ) is rebuilding its C-suite ahead of the new year.

The home improvement retailer said Tuesday that CFO Richard McPhail will slide into the CEO role on Nov. 23. He will be the company's seventh CEO in a history that began with Arthur Blank and Bernie Marcus as co-founders in 1978.

Current CEO Ted Decker will transition to the chairman of the board role.

McPhail takes the leadership baton at HD amid the backdrop of a US housing market he has called "frozen" in the recent past.

"First of all, our customers are the homeowner — and so they're one of the most resilient customer cohorts in the economy," McPhail told Yahoo Finance in a February 2026 interview. "But they're feeling pressure like everyone else. They tell us they have concerns around housing affordability, general affordability, and broader concerns over uncertainty and job loss. So there is pressure on the market. If you look at housing turnover, that's actually been frozen for three years; we have been at historical lows in housing turnover for three years in a row."

He has spent more than 21 years at Home Depot.

He has held the CFO role for more than seven years and also leads the "Pro Acceleration" office, which is focused on improving services for professional Home Depot shoppers.

He started his career in 1996 as an investment banking associate specializing in private equity and M&A at Wachovia Securities. He moved to the corporate finance function at Arthur Anderson in 1998.

He moved to London for five years to work at Marconi Corp in corporate finance.

He is a graduate of Duke University (MBA) and North Carolina State University (BA)

He is known to be a golf and fishing fan.

articles.title: Louzán: "La final del Mundial 2030 sólo puede ser en España y va a ser en España"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la RFEF defiende que la final se dispute en Madrid o Barcelona, anuncia que se estudian los precios de las entradas y apuesta por recuperar Vigo y Valencia como sedes
articles.summary: El presidente de la RFEF defiende que la final se dispute en Madrid o Barcelona, anuncia que se estudian los precios de las entradas y apuesta por recuperar Vigo y Valencia como sedes
articles.body: Rafael Louzán fue uno de los grandes protagonistas de la IV edición del Expansión & Marca Business Sport Forum celebrado en el Espacio La Salle de la madrileña calle San Juan de la Salle. El presidente de la Federación Española, en diálogo con Juan Ignacio Gallardo, director de MARCA, repasó la actualidad de nuestro fútbol con especial atención al momento que viven las selecciones absolutas masculina y femenina, vigentes campeonas del mundo, y, lógicamente, a la organización del próximo Mundial 2030. Y, ahí, fue donde Louzán dejó claras las intenciones españolas en torno a la sede de la gran final. "Solo puede ser en España y va a ser en España", aseguró durante su participación en la mesa 'Mundial 2030: El deporte como nueva potencia económica mundial'. El máximo responsable del fútbol español abordó las incógnitas que rodean la organización del torneo, desde la elección del estadio que albergará la final hasta las sedes españolas y el precio de las entradas, además de analizar el impacto económico de los éxitos de la selección. "La cuenta atrás empezó y hay que correr para llegar con las cosas y los trabajos hechos. En Marruecos manda uno solo y aquí a nivel de gobierno mandan varios. Hay que ponerse manos a la obra y es momento de actuar", declaró Louzán. "Este es un Mundial que pertenece al continente europeo", defendió además, y recordó que en el libro de la candidatura presentado en 2024 figuran tres posibles escenarios para la final: el Santiago Bernabéu, el estadio del Barcelona y el de Casablanca. "Yo creo que este tema estaría muy bien que se hubiera cerrado en su momento", lamentó. "Portugal ha declinado, evidentemente, la celebración porque no hay un estadio con capacidad de 80.000 personas para albergar la final. Por lo tanto, solo puede ser en España y va a ser en España", insistió el presidente de la RFEF, que reclamó acelerar una decisión que todavía podría demorarse. "Lo que hay que intentar, ya lo dije con los de FIFA, es cerrar cuanto antes, internamente. Porque la idea, por lo que parece, no se va a cerrar hasta 2028". Otro de los asuntos que más preocupan a Louzán es el precio de las entradas, después de lo sucedido en el Mundial de 2026. "Espero que las entradas no sean tan caras como han sido para la final. Ya se lo dije el otro día a los de FIFA", explicó, después de referirse a localidades que alcanzaron los 5.000 dólares y a otras cuyos precios estaban "en torno a los mil y algo de euros". "Nos hemos quejado de los precios de las entradas", aseguró el presidente, que defendió la necesidad de facilitar el acceso a los aficionados. "Te encuentras a aficionados españoles que llevan 12 o 14 Mundiales, gente de Murcia, de Menorca, de Sevilla. Son gente de un poder adquisitivo medio o incluso en algunos casos bajo y, por lo tanto, el fútbol tiene que ser asequible para estas personas". "Nuestros aficionados viajan haciendo escala en no sé cuántos sitios para poder llegar. El fútbol es el deporte más importante de nuestras vidas, en cierta manera, y también debe seguir siendo asequible", añadió. De cara a 2030, Louzán adelantó que ya se ha hablado con la FIFA y que se está trabajando en un estudio económico para determinar los precios de las entradas. "Creo que en este Mundial quizá ahí se nos fue. Pero también la FIFA me contestaba: 'Mira, esta es la carta de presentación, los estadios están llenos'. Estamos en la primera economía del mundo y había que admitirlo. Pero que sepan que para España se está haciendo un estudio económico, porque ya lo hemos hablado, para ver los precios que se van a implantar para el Mundial 2030", concluyó el presidente de la RFEF. En cuanto a las sedes, el presidente de la RFEF confirmó su intención de recuperar dos ciudades: "Teníamos 11, ahora tenemos nueve y vamos a intentar incorporar Vigo y Valencia a esas 11 que tiene España, seis Marruecos y tres Portugal". Sin embargo, advirtió de que todavía no está definido el número definitivo de escenarios mundialistas. "Eso no quiere decir que esas 20 vayan a ser las sedes. Estados Unidos, con el mismo número de selecciones, 48, ha tenido 16. Por lo tanto, España, Marruecos y Portugal, vamos a ver cuántas quedarán: 16, 18, 20... Ahí la dejo". Louzán también reclamó acelerar los preparativos. "Creo que es momento de actuar", señaló, antes de destacar el esfuerzo económico que ya se está realizando: "Ahora mismo se están invirtiendo en los estadios de España cerca de 2.500 millones de euros en mejoras". Una inversión que, según explicó, procede principalmente de clubes, ayuntamientos, comunidades autónomas y diputaciones, y no del Gobierno central. El presidente de la RFEF también abordó la dimensión económica de los éxitos deportivos. "Los premios de ganar el Mundial son un poco más de 50 millones de dólares, lo que es lo mismo, unos 40 y pocos millones de euros. Por haber ganado la Eurocopa eran 32 millones de euros", explicó, aunque recordó que los gastos de desplazamiento y alojamiento del Mundial norteamericano fueron muy superiores a los de la Eurocopa celebrada en Alemania. En materia comercial, Louzán destacó el regreso de grandes patrocinadores como Movistar y la incorporación de marcas como Mapfre o Ebro. "Ahora hay confianza. Probablemente el año que viene llegaremos a doblar los ingresos de patrocinio", adelantó, aclarando que ese crecimiento ya se venía trabajando desde antes de conquistar el Mundial. Por último, el presidente se atrevió incluso a imaginar la final de 2030. "España tiene una selección para poder estar ahí, porque la mayoría de los jugadores que tenemos ahora mismo tienen una media de 24 o 25 años". Y fue más allá al señalar un posible rival: "Un finalista va a ser España, ya que me preguntas. Uno puede ser España y otro puede ser Inglaterra. ¿Por qué no?". Una final que, si se cumplen sus deseos, tendría como escenario Madrid o Barcelona. Louzán intervino a mediodía en un foro que se desarrolló en jornadas de mañana y tarde, patrocinado por la Comunidad de Madrid, IFEMA Madrid, Iberdrola, Unicaja, LaLiga, Ariete, Cellnex, DAZN y Philip Morris España, y en el que la bienvenida corrió a cargo de Ana Isabel Pereda, directora de EXPANSIÓN, y del propio Gallardo, con discurso institucional de Alberto Tomé, director general de Deportes de la Comunidad de Madrid.

articles.title: Nvidia earnings will show if the Bank of Nvidia is still open: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Nvidia started pulling back on lending under Jensen Huang, and Colette Kress inherits a bank that's mostly closed.
articles.body:
Nvidia reports Tuesday with its longtime finance chief, Colette Kress , in charge. The Bank of Nvidia she inherited was already turning customers away.

Wall Street will grade Nvidia ( NVDA ) on chips and guidance after the bell . But the most revealing page may sit in the back of the filing, where Nvidia lists what it has promised to pay or guarantee for others.

That list nearly doubled in a single quarter, JPMorgan's Michael Cembalest noted , and comes to about $530 billion with guarantees included. Huang's exit put that web of deals under the microscope.

The man who built the bank had already started closing its windows.

In August, Nvidia's guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center came in at less than half the $250 billion that had been discussed. By the end of the month, Nvidia had paused revenue-sharing deals with neoclouds — upstart cloud companies that rent out Nvidia chips — The Wall Street Journal reported . In October, Huang told those partners to get their customers to pay upfront.

"You're not charging what you should be charging," he told them at a conference in Berlin, according to the Journal.

Neoclouds may be rooting for a Huang comeback , but his return wouldn't reopen windows he was shutting himself. Kress is expected to tighten the purse strings even further, the Journal reported. The $500 billion lending platform Nvidia launched with Wall Street in August still hasn't closed a deal, and lenders want Nvidia to back more than a quarter of each loan, Bloomberg reported.

"I do expect the company to pivot pretty hard under new leadership," Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, said on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang. "I think we're going to see less circular financing activity. We've already seen a slowdown just in the last three weeks."

The stock market noticed first. CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ) have each lost more than half their value in three months, while Nvidia is down about 30%. Nebius is still up for the year.

Some promises can't be taken back. Deals Nvidia already signed — from chip supply orders to cloud capacity it agreed to rent back — are still owed. And Nvidia is set to buy $10 billion of Anthropic stock alongside the AI lab's IPO , which prices Wednesday, according to Anthropic's amended filing.

That makes Tuesday's report about more than demand. Investors will want to know whether the pile of promises keeps growing, and whether Kress sounds like a banker who's still lending.

David Nelson, chief strategist at Belpointe Asset Management, sees two AI trades hiding inside one. Some companies pay for their data centers out of the cash they earn. Others lean on leases, loan guarantees and "other people's money," as he put it, the kind of help Nvidia has been handing out.

articles.title: Nvidia reports strong third quarter after Huang departs

articles.body:
Nvidia reported strong earnings for the third quarter on Tuesday, less than a week after former CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang left the company .

The chipmaker reported $115.8 billion in revenue from July through September, an increase of 20 percent from the second quarter and 103 percent from the third quarter of 2025.

Through the third quarter of this year, Nvidia has reported $293.6 billion in revenue, as its chips power the AI boom sweeping the globe.

That will go on without Huang, who resigned on Thursday amid reports of his extramarital affairs — including one reportedly with an alleged Chinese spy. Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 and became the face of the AI industry in recent years.

In his first statement since resigning, Huang said Tuesday he made “serious mistakes” in his personal life and “created problems” for the company’s board he “deeply” regrets.

Huang also acknowledged an “outpouring of calls” from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners and customers for him to return as CEO , adding many have reached out to him directly.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he added .

But Nvidia’s Board of Directors is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO, a source familiar confirmed to The Hill on Monday.

Colette Kress, who is filling Huang’s shoes as Nvidia’s interim CEO, said in Tuesday’s earnings release the company’s momentum “is real.”

“NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” added Kress.

Nvidia reported $107.6 billion in data center revenue last quarter, an increase of 21 percent from the second quarter and 110 percent from the third quarter of 2025. Looking ahead to the final quarter of this year, the company projects it will bring in $130 billion in revenue.

Nvidia’s stock , which has slid in recent weeks amid the reports on Huang’s affairs, ticked up during after-hours trading after the company released its third-quarter earnings. The company’s stock is trading at roughly $158 per share, above its closing mark of less than $155.50 per share but still more than $80 below its all-time high of $243.37 reached last month.
